history.heading: Principality of Moldavia
paragraphs: The territory of Moldova was inhabited by Dacians and influenced by Rome. The Principality of Moldavia was founded in the 14th century, covering present-day Moldova and eastern Romania. Under Stephen the Great (1457–1504), it resisted the Ottomans, building many monasteries, but later became an Ottoman vassal.

history.heading: Bessarabia
paragraphs: In 1812 the Russian Empire annexed the eastern half of Moldavia, between the Prut and Dniester rivers, calling it Bessarabia. In 1918 Bessarabia united with Romania. The Soviet Union annexed it in 1940, creating the Moldavian SSR together with a strip of land east of the Dniester (Transnistria). Soviet rule brought deportations and a famine in 1946–47.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: Moldova declared independence on 27 August 1991. A war in 1992 left the Russian-backed region of Transnistria outside government control, with Russian troops still present. Moldova has alternated between pro-Russian and pro-European governments. It became an EU candidate in 2022 and opened accession talks in 2024. A 2024 referendum narrowly approved the goal of EU membership, and pro-European President Maia Sandu was re-elected. Her party kept its majority in 2025.

culture.heading: Language and traditions
paragraphs: The official language is Romanian (officially renamed from "Moldovan" in 2023); Russian is widely spoken, along with Gagauz and Ukrainian. Most people are Orthodox Christian.

Moldova has a long winemaking tradition, with huge underground wine cellars such as Mileștii Mici, the largest in the world by collection. Mărțișor, celebrating spring on 1 March, is recognised by UNESCO. Mămăligă (maize porridge) and plăcinte (pastries) are staples.

politics.heading: Parliamentary republic
paragraphs: Moldova is a parliamentary republic with a directly elected president. Politics is shaped by the struggle between pro-EU and pro-Russian forces; authorities have accused Russia of election interference and vote-buying. The autonomous region of Gagauzia and the breakaway Transnistria are sensitive issues. Moldova is constitutionally neutral.

economy.heading: Europe's poorest country
paragraphs: Moldova is one of the poorest countries in Europe. Agriculture and food processing, including wine, fruits and sunflower oil, are important, along with IT and manufacturing of car parts. Remittances from Moldovans working abroad are significant, and emigration has shrunk the population.
Moldova ended its dependence on Russian gas after 2022. The EU is its main trading partner. The currency is the leu.
